message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"20.1","text":"During the night, he rose, woke us, and sat down as usual. He said, “Ask me about whatever you wish.” Sophonias was the first to begin with him: “Explain to us, since we desire to learn, how the account concerning the evil one really stands.” Peter said, “I have indeed already made it clear through the discussion with Simon, but because the things concerning him were stated together with other points, the matter was not brought to light very clearly. For many points that seem equal in force to the truth give most people some knowledge of the truth itself. Therefore, if I now tell you what I had then told Simon among many points, do not suppose that you have been accorded the same honor as he was.” Sophonias said, “You speak rightly. For if you now separate out for us the matter itself from the many points stated then, you will make the actual truth clearer.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁ περὶ πονηροῦ λόγος","chosen":"the account concerning the evil one","rationale":"The adjective is substantival and refers to the personal evil ruler discussed throughout the following sections; “the matter concerning evil” remains a possible broader nuance."},{"source_quote":"τῷ δὲ σὺν ἑτέροις κεφαλαίοις τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰρηκέναι","chosen":"because the things concerning him were stated together with other points","rationale":"The articular infinitive gives the reason the subject was not made fully clear; κεφάλαια denotes principal points or topics here."},{"source_quote":"μὴ οἰηθῆτε ἴσῃ αὐτῷ τιμῇ τετιμῆσθαι","chosen":"do not suppose that you have been accorded the same honor as he was","rationale":"The omitted subject of the infinitive is understood as the present hearers, and αὐτῷ most naturally refers to Simon. An alternative is to take αὐτῷ as referring to the truth or the preceding material, but Sophonias’s reply supports a contrast between Simon’s mixed presentation and the hearers’ clearer one."},{"source_quote":"ἀφορίζεις","chosen":"separate out","rationale":"The verb means to distinguish or set apart the subject from the many other points previously discussed."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"20.2","text":"Peter said, “Hear, therefore, the truth about the arrangement concerning the evil one. God defined two kingdoms and constituted two ages. He judged that the present world should be given to the evil one because it is small and passes away quickly, but he promised to give the coming age to the good one, since it is great and eternal. He therefore made the human being self-determining, with the capacity to incline toward whatever actions he wishes. His body is three-part and has its origin from the female, for it has desire, anger, grief, and the things that follow these. The spirit—though itself not third in origin but three-part—has its origin from the male and is receptive to reasoning, knowledge, fear, and the things that follow these. Each of the two triads has one root, so that the human being is from two compounds, female and male. For this reason two ways were also set before him, that of law and that of lawlessness. Two kingdoms were also defined: one called the kingdom of the heavens, and the other the kingdom of those now reigning upon the earth. Moreover, two kings were appointed. One is appointed by law to reign over the present and temporary world, and he was blended so as to delight in the destruction of the wicked. The other, himself also being a king (of the age that is to come), loves the whole human race. Unable to possess freedom to speak openly in the present circumstances ..... as one who, trying to keep hidden who he is, counsels what is beneficial.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς περὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἁρμονίας","chosen":"the arrangement concerning the evil one","rationale":"ἁρμονία can denote an arrangement, constitution, or harmonious ordering. “Arrangement” fits the ensuing account of two ages, kingdoms, rulers, and elemental mixtures; “composition” is also possible in view of the later blending language."},{"source_quote":"αὐτεξούσιον","chosen":"self-determining","rationale":"The term describes possessing authority over one’s own choices, not unlimited power."},{"source_quote":"οὐ τριτογενὲς ὄν, ἀλλὰ τριμερές","chosen":"not third in origin but three-part","rationale":"The contrast distinguishes being third-generated or third in derivation from being divided into three parts. The more literal “not third-born” is possible but less clear in English."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ φυραμάτων δύο","chosen":"from two compounds","rationale":"φυράματα literally evokes kneaded masses or mixtures; “compounds” preserves the author’s composite anthropology without importing a more familiar theological formulation."},{"source_quote":"νόμῳ βασιλεύειν χειροτονεῖται","chosen":"is appointed by law to reign","rationale":"χειροτονέω can mean choose or appoint, while νόμῳ indicates that the appointment and rule are lawful."},{"source_quote":"ἐπ’ ὀλέθρῳ πονηρῶν χαίρειν ἐκράθη","chosen":"was blended so as to delight in the destruction of the wicked","rationale":"ἐκράθη is retained as compositional or blending language because the following section explains the rulers through elemental mixture."},{"source_quote":"τὴν παρρησίαν ἔχειν","chosen":"to possess freedom to speak openly","rationale":"παρρησία can mean boldness, freedom of speech, or openness. The following attempt to remain concealed favors the sense of acting or speaking openly."},{"source_quote":"τίς ποτ’ ἔστι λανθάνειν πειρώμενος","chosen":"trying to keep hidden who he is","rationale":"The indirect question τίς ποτ’ ἔστι is taken as what the king attempts to conceal. Alternatively, the words could describe him more generally as trying to escape notice."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐν τοῖς παροῦσι τὴν παρρησίαν ἔχειν οὐ δυνάμενος ..... ὧς","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly five dots. Its unavailable content has not been restored, and the five dots are retained in the English.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὧς, τίς ποτ’ ἔστι λανθάνειν πειρώμενος","issue":"The circumflexed form ὧς is difficult in this construction and may be an accentual error for the conjunction ὡς. The main text renders the context as a comparison while preserving the adjacent printed lacuna.","proposed_reading":"ὡς, τίς ποτ’ ἔστι λανθάνειν πειρώμενος","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.3","text":"“Of these two ..... compels the other at God’s command. Each person has authority ........... thus to obey whichever of them he wishes, with a view to doing good or evil. If someone chooses to do good things, he becomes the possession of the good king who is to come. But if someone should do base things, he becomes an instrument of the present evil one. Through sin, the latter has received authority against him by a just judgment; and wishing to act even before the coming age, he delights in punishing him in the present life and, while gratifying his own desire, carries out God’s will. The other was created to delight in authority over righteous people. When he finds a righteous person, he rejoices greatly, saving him for eternal life; and he too, as though gratifying himself, offers God the thanks for these things. Every unjust person may be saved after regretting his course, and every righteous man may incur punishment for a final sin. But these two rulers are God’s swift hands, eager to act beforehand in carrying out his will. That this is so is also stated in the law in the person of God: ‘I will kill and make alive; I will strike, and I too will heal.’ For he truly kills and gives life. He kills through the left hand, that is, through the evil one who was blended so as to delight in the affliction of the impious. But he saves and benefits through the right hand, that is, through the good one who was created to delight in benefiting and saving the righteous. These have their substances not from outside God, for there is no other first principle. Yet they were not brought forth by God as living beings, for then they would have shared his disposition. Nor did they arise accidentally, having come into being spontaneously contrary to his purpose, since then the greatest extent of his power would have been abolished. Rather, the four primary elements were brought forth from God: hot and cold, wet and dry. Thus he is in fact the father of every substance ..... with disposition being what arises after the blending; for when they were blended outside, choice was born as their offspring. The evil one, therefore, after serving God blamelessly until the end of the present world, can, since he is not of a single substance—that of permanence in evil—become good when recombined. For even now he does nothing evil, although he is evil, since he has lawfully received authority to inflict suffering.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"κτῆμα","chosen":"possession","rationale":"The word denotes something acquired or owned and presents the person as belonging to the coming good king."},{"source_quote":"ὑπηρέτημα","chosen":"instrument","rationale":"The formation denotes something that serves or ministers. “Instrument” preserves its contrast with κτῆμα, though “servant” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"μεταμεληθέντι","chosen":"after regretting his course","rationale":"The verb denotes regret or a change of concern and is kept distinct from the μετανόησις terminology for moral-spiritual reorientation. In context the regret is understood to result in abandoning injustice."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τελευταίας ἁμαρτίας","chosen":"for a final sin","rationale":"τελευταίας may describe one last sin or a sin committed at the end of life. The singular rendering follows the morphology while leaving the temporal nuance possible."},{"source_quote":"ταχεῖαι χεῖρές εἰσι θεοῦ","chosen":"are God’s swift hands","rationale":"The bodily image is preserved directly rather than reduced to “agents.”"},{"source_quote":"προλαμβάνειν ἐπιθυμοῦσαι τὸ αὐτοῦ θέλημα ἐπιτελεῖν","chosen":"eager to act beforehand in carrying out his will","rationale":"προλαμβάνειν conveys anticipation or acting in advance; the rulers execute divine judgment or benefit before its final fulfillment."},{"source_quote":"ὁμόδοξοι γὰρ αὐτῷ ἦσαν","chosen":"for then they would have shared his disposition","rationale":"ὁμόδοξος means holding the same opinion or disposition, not possessing the same glory. The counterfactual force is supplied by the argument’s context."},{"source_quote":"συμβεβήκασιν","chosen":"did they arise accidentally","rationale":"The perfect verb can mean simply “happened,” but here it contrasts intended derivation from God with spontaneous accidental occurrence."},{"source_quote":"ἔξω γὰρ κραθεῖσιν αὐτοῖς","chosen":"for when they were blended outside","rationale":"ἔξω is retained without supplying an explicit object. It may mean outside God or externally to the original divine bringing-forth."},{"source_quote":"ἅτε δὴ οὐ μιᾶς οὐσίας ὢν τῆς πρὸς κακίαν μονῆς μετασυγκριθεὶς ἀγαθὸς γενέσθαι δύναται","chosen":"since he is not of a single substance—that of permanence in evil—can become good when recombined","rationale":"The genitive phrase is taken as characterizing the single substance the evil one does not possess, while μετασυγκριθείς denotes recomposition. Alternatively, τῆς πρὸς κακίαν μονῆς may attach more directly to the recombination and describe release from persistence in evil."},{"source_quote":"νομίμως κακουχεῖν εἰληφὼς τὴν ἐξουσίαν","chosen":"since he has lawfully received authority to inflict suffering","rationale":"The claim is that his punitive action is authorized, preserving the author’s distinction between being evil and acting outside the assigned law."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τῶν δὲ δύο τούτων ..... τὸν ἕτερον ἐκβιάζεται","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly five dots where the grammatical subject or other governing wording may have stood. No subject has been restored in the English, which retains the sentence fragment and all five dots.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐξουσίαν ἔχει........... ὥ αὐτῶν ᾧ βούλεται πείθεσθαι","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly eleven dots, retained in the English. The surviving ὥ is syntactically difficult before αὐτῶν ᾧ and may be defective; the main text represents it minimally as “thus” rather than silently supplying additional Greek.","proposed_reading":"ἐξουσίαν ἔχει........... ὥστε αὐτῶν ᾧ βούλεται πείθεσθαι","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὅθεν δὴ καὶ πατὴρ τυγχάνει πάσης οὐσίας ..... οὔσης γνώμης τῆς μετὰ τὴν κρᾶσιν","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly five dots between the statement about God as father of every substance and the genitive phrase about disposition. No connective or missing claim has been supplied, and the five dots remain explicit.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.4","text":"After Peter said these things, Micah, who was also one of the followers, asked, “What, then, is the source of human sin?” Peter said, “It comes from not knowing that, when judgment has taken place concerning the things they do wrongly, they are certain to be punished. Consequently, although they possess desire for the continuation of life—as I said on another occasion—they satisfy it indiscriminately, through the corruption of half-grown boys or through some other flattering sin. Because they do not know that they are judged, as I said before, they hasten through their lack of fear to satisfy desire unlawfully. Thus God is not evil, for he established desire well so that there might be continuation of life. Rather, they themselves are most impious, since they have used what is good in desire badly. The same reasoning may also be applied to anger: someone who uses it justly, as is permitted, acts piously, but one who goes beyond the proper measure and takes judgment into his own hands acts impiously.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"κρίσεως γενομένης","chosen":"when judgment has taken place","rationale":"The genitive absolute places punishment after judgment concerning the wrongful acts."},{"source_quote":"διαδοχὴν βίου","chosen":"the continuation of life","rationale":"The expression refers to the succession or perpetuation of human life through generation."},{"source_quote":"ταύτην πληροφοροῦσιν ὡς ἔτυχεν","chosen":"they satisfy it indiscriminately","rationale":"πληροφορέω here means bring desire to fulfillment or satisfy it, while ὡς ἔτυχεν means casually, haphazardly, or without proper distinction."},{"source_quote":"ἤμ[ιπεπείρων] παίδων","chosen":"half-grown boys","rationale":"The bracketed form denotes boys who are half-mature or not yet fully grown; “adolescent boys” is a smoother alternative but loses the source’s ripening image."},{"source_quote":"κολακευούσῃ ἁμαρτίᾳ","chosen":"flattering sin","rationale":"The participle portrays the sin as flattering or pandering to desire. “Self-indulgent sin” would express the implication more dynamically."},{"source_quote":"τῷ καλῷ τῆς ἐπιθυμίας χρησάμενοι κακῶς","chosen":"they have used what is good in desire badly","rationale":"The wording distinguishes desire’s good divinely assigned function from its wrongful human use."},{"source_quote":"ἑαυτῷ τὴν κρίσιν λαβὼν","chosen":"takes judgment into his own hands","rationale":"The idiom conveys assuming for oneself the authority to judge or punish."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"κρί[σεως γε]νομένης","issue":"The selected edition places σεως γε in square brackets within the phrase. The translation follows the resulting printed reading while disclosing its editorially marked status; no further restoration is proposed.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"εἶ[πον]","issue":"The selected edition places πον in square brackets to complete the verb. The translation follows the bracketed reading “I said.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"[εἰς] διαδοχὴν βίου","issue":"The preposition εἰς is printed in square brackets. The translation follows the selected edition’s bracketed construction without claiming that the brackets recover independently verified wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἤμ[ιπεπείρων] παίδων","issue":"Most of the adjective is printed in square brackets, and the resulting spelling is unusual beside standard ἡμιπέπειρος. The contextual sense “half-grown” is defensible, but the editorially marked letters remain uncertain.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.5","text":"Sophonias spoke again: “Your patience, my lord Peter, grants us boldness to ask you many questions for the sake of precision. Therefore, taking courage, we conduct the examination in every way. I remember, then, that yesterday, while Simon was engaged in inquiry with you, he said that if the evil one was generated from God, it follows that he shares the same substance as the one who brought him forth and ought to have been good, not evil. You answered that this does not necessarily follow, since many evil people are born from good people. In the same way, two who were unlike each other were born from Adam, one of whom was evil and the other good. When Simon objected that you had used human examples, you answered that by this reasoning one should not accept that God begets either, for this too is a human example. But I, Sophonias, accept that God begets; I do not accept that he begets evil, even if good people among human beings beget evil children. And do not suppose that I irrationally ascribe to God some things characteristic of human beings but not others, because I concede begetting to him but do not ascribe to him the begetting of what is unlike him. Human beings naturally beget sons whose dispositions are unlike their own for the following reason: because they are composed of four parts, their bodies vary in different ways with different changes, and as the distinctive element of the change at each particular time increases or decreases in a human body, it disrupts the balanced mixture. Because the compounds do not always remain the same, the seeds are secreted at different times with different mixtures, and dispositions, whether good or evil, follow them in accordance with the mixture at that time. But in God’s case no such thing can be conceived, for since he is unchangeable and always existent, wh...... he might wish to bring forth, it is altogether necessary that what is brought forth by him should likewise ...... in every respect in relation to the one who begot it—I mean both substance and disposition. But if anyone should wish to call even him changeable, I do not know how he can also call him immortal.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἡ μακροθυμία σου","chosen":"your patience","rationale":"μακροθυμία denotes forbearance or patience, here Peter’s willingness to endure extensive questioning."},{"source_quote":"παρρησίαν ἡμῖν χαρίζεται","chosen":"grants us boldness","rationale":"Here παρρησία is the confidence or freedom to question Peter openly rather than specifically public speech."},{"source_quote":"ἀκολούθως τῆς αὐτῆς τῷ προβαλόντι τυγχάνει οὐσίας","chosen":"it follows that he shares the same substance as the one who brought him forth","rationale":"ἀκολούθως marks Simon’s inference, while προβάλλω is rendered “bring forth” to preserve the argument about derivation without imposing the technical term “emanation.”"},{"source_quote":"ἀνόμοιοί τινες ὄντες δύο ἐγεννήθησαν","chosen":"two who were unlike each other were born","rationale":"The contrast between the evil and good sons favors mutual dissimilarity, though the phrase could also mean that they were unlike Adam in different respects."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀνθρώποις διαφερόντων","chosen":"things characteristic of human beings","rationale":"The expression concerns features found among or pertaining to humans. “Things in which humans differ” is grammatically possible but fits the argument less well."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὰς διαφόρους τροπὰς διαφόρως τρέπονται τὰ σώματα","chosen":"their bodies vary in different ways with different changes","rationale":"The repeated wordplay between τροπάς and τρέπονται is represented with “changes” and “vary”; the changes may include seasonal or elemental alterations."},{"source_quote":"τὸ τῆς τροπῆς ἴδιον","chosen":"the distinctive element of the change","rationale":"The phrase denotes the quality or component proper to a particular bodily change, likely one of the four elemental qualities."},{"source_quote":"τὰ σπέρματα ἄλλοτε ἄλλην ἔχοντα κρᾶσιν ἀποκρίνονται","chosen":"the seeds are secreted at different times with different mixtures","rationale":"ἀποκρίνονται has the physiological sense of being separated or secreted, while κρᾶσις continues the author’s language of elemental mixture."},{"source_quote":"ἄτρεπτον","chosen":"unchangeable","rationale":"The adjective directly contrasts God with the changing bodily mixtures described immediately before it."},{"source_quote":"τήν τε οὐσίαν λέγω καὶ τὴν γνώμην","chosen":"I mean both substance and disposition","rationale":"γνώμη here denotes disposition, purpose, or cast of mind. “Opinion” is lexically possible but too narrow for the contrast between good and evil offspring."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὅπ...... προβάλλειν βουληθείη","issue":"The selected edition preserves only the fragment ὅπ before a lacuna of exactly six dots. The English represents the incomplete relative or temporal stem as “wh......” and does not complete it as “whatever,” “whenever,” or another conjecture.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τὸ προβαλλόμενον αὐτῷ ὡσαύτως ...... τὰ πάντα τῷ γεγεννηκότι","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly six dots where wording governing the comparison with the begetter is unavailable. The English retains all six dots and does not supply a verb such as “resemble.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"εἰ [δὲ θελήσ]ειέ τις","issue":"The selected edition prints δὲ θελήσ in square brackets, completing the conditional expression. The translation follows that marked reading without proposing additional text.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
